key_insight: Neural PDE solvers can drive the loss toward its optimum while their parameters diverge, revealing that some limiting solutions are not representable in the original finite network class.
engineering_relevance: For PDE surrogate models, this means training may appear successful even when the model class cannot actually realize the best solution, so architecture design and convergence checks must account for missing limits.
method: Analyze deep tanh networks for singular parameter growth and redundant neurons.
Characterize the “missing” limit functions for translated-kernel models.
Complete the hypothesis space by adding kernel derivatives so the best approximation becomes attainable.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical studies that track parameter growth and test how model completion changes PDE optimization behavior.
watch_item: Adding derivative-based completion can improve attainability, but it may increase model complexity and require careful numerical conditioning.
paper_title: Singular parameters and missing limits in neural PDE solvers
